evidence_classes.A: Primary official documentation, standard, specification, SDK, or project source.
evidence_classes.B: First-party engineering report, model/product announcement, or detailed implementation account.
evidence_classes.C: Independent research, benchmark, or established practitioner synthesis.
evidence_classes.D: User-provided artifact used as a design/process input rather than an external factual authority.

sources.key_finding: Codex uses isolated worktrees, skills, automations, sandboxing, and parallel agent surfaces.
sources.operationalization: Require artifact isolation, scoped parallelism, and reusable skills rather than transcript-only guidance.

sources.source: OpenAI — Codex for every role, tool, and workflow
sources.key_finding: Codex expands beyond code edits to hosted artifacts, sites, annotations, and broader workflows.
sources.operationalization: Make the exact durable artifact and its user-facing verification the unit of completion.

sources.source: OpenAI — Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.key_finding: Agent-first engineering shifts effort toward environment design, repository legibility, intent specification, feedback loops, and verification.
sources.operationalization: Center the plugin on layer ownership, repository readiness, harness design, and evidence-backed completion.

sources.source: OpenAI — An open-source spec for Codex orchestration: Symphony
sources.key_finding: Issue trackers and durable work objects can serve as control planes for always-on coding-agent orchestration.
sources.operationalization: Provide issue-to-artifact, durable plan, ownership, and handoff protocols.

sources.source: OpenAI — The next evolution of the Agents SDK
sources.key_finding: The harness can be separated from sandboxed compute for security, durability, and scale.
sources.operationalization: Separate control plane, execution plane, permissions, run state, and effects in harness blueprints.

sources.key_finding: High-quality tasks specify goal, context, constraints, and done-when; reusable guidance belongs in AGENTS.md and plans.
sources.operationalization: Ship execution-contract, layered AGENTS.md, plan, and evidence templates.

sources.key_finding: Skills use progressive disclosure and may package focused instructions, references, assets, and scripts.
sources.operationalization: Use a narrow router plus focused skills; keep deep material in references and deterministic checks in scripts.

sources.source: OpenAI — Testing Agent Skills Systematically with Evals
sources.key_finding: Reusable skills need systematic trigger and behavior evaluations derived from realistic failures.
sources.operationalization: Include should/should-not-trigger cases, behavior contracts, scenarios, and failure-derived eval guidance.

sources.key_finding: Structured boundaries, approvals, guardrails, and trace-based evaluation reduce prompt-injection and unsafe-action risk.
sources.operationalization: Encode provenance separation, capability/approval policies, and safety/recovery evals.

sources.source: OpenAI — A practical guide to building AI agents
sources.key_finding: Agent systems combine model, tools, instructions, guardrails, and orchestration; single-agent simplicity is often preferable.
sources.operationalization: Apply smallest-fitting-architecture escalation and make multi-agent an earned choice.

sources.source: Martin Fowler — Harness engineering for coding agent users
sources.key_finding: Harnesses combine feedforward guides and feedback sensors around coding agents.
sources.operationalization: Use explicit control/feedback mechanisms and distinguish prompt advice from executable controls.

sources.key_finding: AGENTS.md is an open repository convention for instructions to coding agents.
sources.operationalization: Provide layered AGENTS.md guidance and promotion rules for repeated corrections.

sources.key_finding: Workflows have predefined paths while agents adapt their process; simple composable patterns should be preferred.
sources.operationalization: Define architecture escalation from direct call and deterministic workflow to bounded loop, graph, and multi-agent.

sources.source: Anthropic — Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.key_finding: Context is a finite attention budget; high-signal retrieval, curation, provenance, and compaction matter more than maximal volume.
sources.operationalization: Add context classes, retrieval policy, progressive disclosure, and compaction checkpoints.

sources.source: Anthropic — Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.key_finding: Long-running work benefits from initialization, progress files, compaction, resumable state, and fresh-session continuation.
sources.operationalization: Provide durable plan/handoff formats and state/checkpoint requirements.

sources.key_finding: Concise repository guidance, verification loops, hooks/permissions, and scoped parallel work improve coding-agent outcomes.
sources.operationalization: Require fast/full validation, concise guidance, ownership, and fresh verification while avoiding default privileged hooks.

sources.source: Anthropic — Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.key_finding: Multi-turn agents require evaluation of trajectories, graders, environments, and lifecycle behavior, not only final answers.
sources.operationalization: Split outcome, trajectory, recovery, safety, and operational evals.

sources.source: Anthropic — Writing effective tools for AI agents
sources.key_finding: Tool names, descriptions, schemas, examples, boundaries, and tool-specific evals materially affect agent behavior.
sources.operationalization: Ship a semantic tool contract with schemas, effects, errors, permissions, and adversarial tests.

sources.source: Anthropic — Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
sources.key_finding: Modular procedural knowledge can be packaged for progressive, reusable agent capability.
sources.operationalization: Keep skill jobs narrow and place depth in local references/assets.

sources.source: Anthropic — How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.key_finding: Multi-agent systems require careful decomposition, independent work, coordination, integration, evaluation, and cost control.
sources.operationalization: Gate multi-agent use and provide delegation, ownership, fan-in, partial-failure, and coordination metrics.

sources.key_finding: Explicit state graphs can combine deterministic and model-driven nodes with persistence and human-in-the-loop execution.
sources.operationalization: Define state/node/edge contracts and use graphs only when consequential control flow must be explicit.

sources.key_finding: Graph APIs expose state, nodes, edges, reducers, branches, joins, and super-step execution.
sources.operationalization: Provide reducer, join, edge, node, and graph verification contracts.

sources.key_finding: Checkpointers preserve thread state while stores support broader memory; durability has explicit state semantics.
sources.operationalization: Separate checkpoints from memory/cache and require versioned state/replay tests.

sources.key_finding: Interrupts persist state and resume later; code before an interrupt may replay and must be idempotent.
sources.operationalization: Split prepare/approve/execute, validate stale resumes, and test replay around interrupts.

sources.key_finding: At-least-once activity execution requires granular, idempotent effects and stable keys.
sources.operationalization: Require action IDs, effect journals, idempotency and reconciliation around external effects.

sources.key_finding: Killing/restarting workers tests replay, idempotency, retries, and recovery before production.
sources.operationalization: Include crash-point and replay fault matrices for graphs and Rust runtimes.

sources.key_finding: MCP tools use JSON Schema and model-controlled invocation but require validation, access control, clear user visibility, timeouts, logging, and safe output handling.
sources.operationalization: Encode schema-first tools, server-side authorization, approval visibility, output sanitation, and MCP conformance.

sources.key_finding: A2A defines interoperable agent discovery, task lifecycle, artifacts, identity, and enterprise controls.
sources.operationalization: Treat A2A as a peer-agent boundary with durable task mapping, identity, cancellation, and conformance tests.

sources.source: A2A Protocol — A2A and MCP comparison
sources.key_finding: MCP primarily addresses agent-to-tool/resource integration while A2A addresses peer-agent interaction.
sources.operationalization: Keep tool and peer-agent boundaries distinct and do not adopt either protocol without a real interoperability need.

sources.source: Google Agent Development Kit — workflow agents
sources.key_finding: Sequential, parallel, and loop agents provide deterministic orchestration patterns.
sources.operationalization: Distinguish deterministic workflows/fan-out from adaptive loops and multi-agent systems.

sources.key_finding: Typed routing, graph workflows, checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop are first-class orchestration concerns.
sources.operationalization: Require typed routes, checkpoints, interrupts, and verification matrices.

sources.key_finding: Spec-driven development packages constitution, specification, planning, tasks, and implementation for coding agents.
sources.operationalization: Provide an execution contract, architecture brief, plan, ADR, and acceptance matrix.

sources.source: GitHub Spec Kit — Agentic SDD reference
sources.key_finding: Agentic SDD separates clarify, plan, checklist, tasks, analysis, implementation, and convergence.
sources.operationalization: Use phase-specific artifacts and make convergence evidence explicit.

sources.key_finding: Human-validated real GitHub issue-to-patch tasks provide a more reliable coding benchmark subset.
sources.operationalization: Prefer repository-grounded, exact-task eval fixtures and accepted-artifact evidence.

sources.key_finding: Terminal-environment tasks test practical execution across software and systems domains.
sources.operationalization: Evaluate tools, trajectories, state, and environment interaction—not only text generation.

sources.key_finding: Model reliability varies with task duration and should be represented as curves/distributions rather than a single capability claim.
sources.operationalization: Calibrate autonomy and verification to task horizon; avoid treating model capability as deterministic.

sources.key_finding: Coding-agent evaluation should include repository Q&A, tests, refactoring, and work beyond issue resolution.
sources.operationalization: Broaden eval scenarios across architecture, verification, maintenance, and repository understanding.

sources.key_finding: Agentic systems introduce risks across identity, tools, memory, protocols, actions, governance, and supply chains.
sources.operationalization: Ship a threat model, injection/provenance policy, capability/approval controls, and incident protocol.

sources.key_finding: Emerging conventions standardize telemetry vocabulary for model and agent operations.
sources.operationalization: Align trace events where practical while versioning an internal semantic/evidence schema and protecting sensitive data.

sources.key_finding: Structured, bounded agent-generated interfaces are an emerging direction for agent-to-user interaction.
sources.operationalization: Treat interactive approvals and artifacts as explicit contracts rather than unconstrained generated UI.

sources.key_finding: MCP-backed apps can add interactive user surfaces to tool integrations.
sources.operationalization: Keep UI optional and consequence-focused; the plugin ships instruction assets without mandatory connectors or apps.

sources.key_finding: A six-gate method separates situation, evidence, divergence, commitment, interaction contract, and verification with calibrated confidence.
sources.operationalization: Reuse evidence traceability, explicit decision commitment, behavior contracts, and release-gate discipline for this plugin.

sources.source: OpenAI — GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
sources.key_finding: GPT-5.6 adds stronger coding and tool-heavy programmatic execution that can coordinate tools, process intermediate results, and choose next actions.
sources.operationalization: Optimize prompts for decision-complete contracts, typed tools, programmatic aggregation, and evidence-backed stopping.

sources.key_finding: GPT-5.6 Sol is the flagship Codex model for complex coding, computer use, research, and cybersecurity; medium is the default power setting and deeper effort is available.
sources.operationalization: Ship a Sol operating profile and reserve high/Max/Ultra for named complexity rather than using maximum effort by default.

sources.key_finding: Skill metadata is discovered before full instructions; concise front-loaded trigger descriptions and focused jobs improve selection.
sources.operationalization: Create focused skills with trigger-oriented descriptions, negative activation boundaries, named output contracts, and deep local references; split broad domains when activation conditions or decision artifacts differ.

sources.key_finding: A skill is a focused reusable workflow; a plugin is an installable bundle that can combine skills and connectors/MCP.
sources.operationalization: Package the operationalization as an installable plugin while keeping external connectors optional.

sources.key_finding: Codex plugins use a manifest and can package skills under a marketplace structure for installation and sharing.
sources.operationalization: Follow the current `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `skills/`, and marketplace layout and validate it statically.

sources.key_finding: Codex reads AGENTS.md before work and applies layered repository guidance.
sources.operationalization: Provide layered AGENTS.md pattern and keep stable rules out of per-task prompts.

sources.key_finding: Codex can spawn specialized parallel agents and collect their results; this is most useful for highly parallel work.
sources.operationalization: Require explicit delegation, ownership, evidence, fan-in, cancellation, and a multi-agent entry gate.

sources.source: OpenAI — Unrolling the Codex agent loop
sources.key_finding: The Codex harness implements an iterative user/model/tool loop with context assembly and execution logic.
sources.operationalization: Make observe/plan/act/verify/update and tool/effect state explicit instead of relying on a vague iterative prompt.

sources.source: OpenAI — Unlocking the Codex harness: how we built the App Server
sources.key_finding: The Codex harness includes thread persistence, configuration/authentication, tool execution, skills, sandboxing, and a stable event stream through App Server.
sources.operationalization: Treat lifecycle, state, tools, extensions, configuration, authentication, and events as harness concerns.

sources.source: OpenAI — The next evolution of the Agents SDK
sources.key_finding: Separating harness from compute supports controlled sandbox execution and long-horizon work.
sources.operationalization: Keep execution identities and sandboxes separate from the control plane and persist state outside ephemeral workers.

sources.key_finding: Skills are discoverable, reusable workflows with richer instructions, scripts, and references without loading all content up front.
sources.operationalization: Use progressive disclosure and avoid monolithic always-on guidance.

sources.key_finding: Codex surfaces, plugin management, permissions, subagent visibility, and model support evolve rapidly.
sources.operationalization: Add a research/update policy and avoid hard-coding unstable availability or UI details beyond the research lock.

sources.key_finding: Graceful shutdown combines detection, cancellation tokens, and waiting for tasks to finish.
sources.operationalization: Require stop-intake, cancellation propagation, tracked drain, reconciliation, persistence, and a final deadline.

sources.key_finding: Tokio schedules async tasks cooperatively; blocking or non-yielding work can stall core threads and runtime lifetime has explicit semantics.
sources.operationalization: Separate blocking work, supervise tasks, and make task/runtime ownership explicit.

sources.key_finding: Semaphores bound concurrent access by permits and await capacity.
sources.operationalization: Use per-resource bounded concurrency with cancellation/deadlines and overload metrics.

sources.key_finding: `cargo check` type-checks packages without final code generation and is faster, but some code-generation errors remain outside its coverage.
sources.operationalization: Use `cargo check` as an early gate, not a substitute for tests and release builds.

sources.key_finding: `cargo test` compiles and runs unit, integration, and documentation tests.
sources.operationalization: Include workspace/unit/integration/doc tests in the verification ladder.

sources.key_finding: Clippy is an official toolchain component for additional lint analysis.
sources.operationalization: Include project-policy Clippy checks and do not claim unavailable linting passed.

sources.key_finding: Rustfmt is an official toolchain component invoked through Cargo for formatting.
sources.operationalization: Include deterministic format checks in fast and release gates.

sources.source: The Cargo Book — cargo miri / Miri
sources.key_finding: Miri runs compatible binaries/tests in an interpreter and can detect classes of undefined behavior; it is a nightly optional component.
sources.operationalization: Use Miri selectively for unsafe/FFI-sensitive code and report it separately from ordinary tests.

sources.key_finding: Loom explores concurrent executions of small synchronization tests using state reduction.
sources.operationalization: Use Loom for narrow concurrency primitives while retaining integration and process fault tests.

sources.key_finding: RustSec provides a vulnerability advisory database and tooling such as cargo-audit for Cargo.lock.
sources.operationalization: Include dependency advisory/exception policy and exact artifact provenance in CI guidance.

sources.key_finding: Cargo documents build/check/test patterns for CI and highlights target/version considerations.
sources.operationalization: Provide PR/release verification matrices rather than one local command.

sources.source: Model Context Protocol — official Rust SDK
sources.key_finding: The official Rust SDK supports building MCP clients and servers exposing tools, resources, and prompts.
sources.operationalization: Keep MCP in an adapter crate, validate/authorize server-side, and run protocol/security conformance tests.

sources.key_finding: The Rust workspace implements A2A v1 protocol types plus async client/server and gRPC support.
sources.operationalization: Isolate A2A wire types, map durable task lifecycle, authenticate peers, and test independent interoperability.

sources.key_finding: Rust applications can use a durable execution platform for persisted invocations and workflow/service semantics.
sources.operationalization: Present durable runtime adoption as an option requiring hard-semantics proof, not a default framework dependency.

sources.key_finding: Rust agent frameworks expose tracing/observability integration but application evidence and policy remain separate concerns.
sources.operationalization: Keep framework telemetry behind adapters and require run/action/evidence IDs independent of one framework.

sources.source: Schemars — JSON Schema generation for Rust
sources.key_finding: Schemars derives JSON Schema from Rust types, supporting schema-first protocol/tool surfaces while still requiring review for compatibility and semantics.
sources.operationalization: Provide typed wire DTOs and schema snapshots but require semantic validation and protocol compatibility tests.

sources.key_finding: A production-grade improvement loop starts with real traces, gathers human and model feedback, converts findings into evals, and changes prompts, tools, policy, or harness behavior before re-running the loop.
sources.operationalization: Require a trace-to-change ledger that links field observations to hypotheses, regression fixtures, product or harness changes, rollout evidence, and keep/revert decisions.

sources.source: OpenAI — Macro Evals for Agentic Systems
sources.key_finding: Agentic systems require evaluation across end-to-end outcomes, trajectories, tool behavior, and interaction patterns rather than isolated model responses alone.
sources.operationalization: Make authentic-use evidence joinable to outcome, trajectory, intervention, recovery, and system-version records; use field-derived cases to maintain macro evals.

sources.source: Anthropic — Measuring AI agent autonomy in practice
sources.key_finding: Real use shows autonomy is graded and shaped by task duration, intervention, human oversight, and deployment context; capability does not imply unrestricted authority.
sources.operationalization: Use an autonomy-and-exposure ladder with observed intervention burden, effect risk, and recovery evidence as promotion criteria rather than treating autonomy as binary.

sources.source: Anthropic — Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.key_finding: Useful agent evaluations start from representative tasks and failure modes, combine multiple graders and transcript inspection, and mature through an iterative process rather than a single score.
sources.operationalization: Require task-distribution coverage, grader calibration, trace review, failure-derived regressions, and explicit limits on what offline evals prove.

sources.source: NIST AI 800-4 — A Methodology for Assessing and Managing Post-Deployment AI Risks
sources.key_finding: Post-deployment AI risk management requires continuous monitoring, context-specific impact assessment, incident handling, change management, stakeholder feedback, and documented reassessment as conditions evolve.
sources.operationalization: Make controlled field learning a governed post-deployment assurance activity with operating envelopes, escalation thresholds, observation quality, incident links, and reauthorization after material change.

sources.source: NIST AI RMF — Core and Playbook
sources.key_finding: AI risk work spans Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage and should be continuous, context-sensitive, documented, and connected to human and organizational decision rights.
sources.operationalization: Map lifecycle artifacts and field-learning decisions to governance, context, measurement, and risk-treatment responsibilities rather than treating evaluation as an isolated technical task.

sources.source: Nature Medicine — Silent trials in healthcare AI: a scoping review
sources.key_finding: Silent deployment can test workflow fit, data quality, calibration, integration, and operational behavior without influencing decisions, but inconsistent terminology and reporting limit comparability.
sources.operationalization: Define shadow or silent operation precisely, record exposure and counterfactual outputs, prohibit unapproved effects, and specify evidence required to advance beyond observation-only operation.

sources.source: The silent trial — a bridge from algorithms to clinical practice
sources.key_finding: Prospective silent evaluation reveals performance, implementation, and workflow problems that retrospective validation cannot expose while avoiding direct impact on live decisions.
sources.operationalization: Use prospective shadow-mode trials where risk warrants, with predeclared endpoints, representative workflow coverage, mismatch review, and transition criteria.

sources.source: Microsoft Research — Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation: During-Experiment Stage
sources.key_finding: Trustworthy online experiments require treatment integrity, data-quality checks, trustworthy analysis, monitoring during exposure, and protection against interpretation pitfalls.
sources.operationalization: Require assignment, exposure, outcome, and telemetry integrity checks; freeze decision rules before reading results; stop or invalidate experiments with unresolved data-quality failures.

sources.source: Microsoft Research — Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
sources.key_finding: Sample ratio mismatch is a symptom of assignment, execution, logging, analysis, or survivorship problems and can make apparent treatment effects untrustworthy.
sources.operationalization: Make sample-ratio and exposure-integrity checks blocking experiment gates; diagnose the mechanism before using results for product decisions.

sources.source: Microsoft Research — Pitfalls of Long-Term Online Controlled Experiments
sources.key_finding: Long-running experiments can be distorted by identity instability, survivorship and selection bias, novelty, carryover, and misleading trends.
sources.operationalization: Require long-horizon metric and cohort reasoning, stable assignment analysis, carryover policy, and explicit limits on extrapolating short-term effects.

sources.source: Microsoft Research — Experimentation in Generative AI: C++ Team Practices for Continuous Improvement
sources.key_finding: Generative-AI product development benefits from complementary offline evaluation, online experimentation, qualitative inspection, feedback, and continuous iteration because no single measure captures quality.
sources.operationalization: Combine controlled metrics with trace review and user/workflow evidence; use field failures to update offline datasets and product mechanisms.

sources.key_finding: Software lifecycle work is a set of interrelated technical, management, agreement, and support processes that can be tailored to context and iterated across the life of a system.
sources.operationalization: Represent the lifecycle as an assurance network with tailored decisions, artifacts, evidence, roles, and feedback paths rather than a mandatory waterfall.

sources.key_finding: Systems engineering spans conception through utilization, support, and retirement, integrating stakeholder needs, architecture, verification, validation, transition, operation, and disposal.
sources.operationalization: Keep product, software, operational, support, and retirement decisions connected; require mission threads and lifecycle-wide evidence continuity.

sources.key_finding: Good requirements are derived from stakeholder needs and operational concepts, are traceable and verifiable, and include interfaces, constraints, and quality attributes.
sources.operationalization: Create operational concepts, mission threads, requirement quality checks, bidirectional traceability, verification methods, and controlled baselines.

sources.key_finding: Software and ICT product quality is multi-dimensional; functional correctness alone does not establish reliability, security, compatibility, usability, maintainability, or other quality characteristics.
sources.operationalization: Use explicit quality-attribute scenarios and evidence plans so agent-generated software is not judged only by feature completion or passing unit tests.

sources.key_finding: Lifecycle management requires selection and tailoring of processes, integrated planning, decision management, configuration control, information management, measurement, and risk management.
sources.operationalization: Require lifecycle tailoring, decision records, baselines, evidence ownership, measurements, and change triggers across all plugin lifecycle skills.

sources.source: Software Engineering Institute — Quality Attribute Workshop Collection
sources.key_finding: Stakeholder-driven quality-attribute scenarios make vague nonfunctional concerns concrete through stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and response measure.
sources.operationalization: Require measurable quality-attribute scenarios before architecture commitments and use them as construction, test, and production evidence targets.

sources.source: Software Engineering Institute — Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method
sources.key_finding: Architecture evaluation should expose quality-attribute tradeoffs, sensitivity points, risks, non-risks, and assumptions before costs are locked in.
sources.operationalization: Use explicit tradeoff analysis and risk themes to prioritize thin slices, spikes, and evidence rather than selecting architecture by fashion or agent preference.

sources.source: GOV.UK Service Manual — How the discovery phase works
sources.key_finding: Discovery is for understanding the problem, users, constraints, current journeys, risks, and whether a service should proceed—not for prematurely building the solution.
sources.operationalization: Require representative research, current-state evidence, problem framing, assumptions, constraints, and a go/stop recommendation before deeper implementation.

sources.source: GOV.UK Service Manual — How the beta phase works
sources.key_finding: Beta builds and improves a working service in small releases, learns from real users, manages operational readiness, and addresses accessibility, security, performance, and support needs.
sources.operationalization: Use thin vertical slices, controlled real-use exposure, progressive delivery, operational readiness, and recurring evidence reviews before broader release.

sources.source: GOV.UK Service Manual — Retiring your service
sources.key_finding: Service retirement requires user communication, migration or alternatives, data and dependency handling, support planning, and evidence that critical journeys remain protected.
sources.operationalization: Treat retirement as an engineered lifecycle phase with owner, inventory, communication, migration, rollback, evidence retention, and post-close verification.

sources.key_finding: Human-AI systems should set expectations, support efficient invocation, make uncertainty and limits legible, allow correction and dismissal, learn cautiously, and support global controls.
sources.operationalization: Include expectation, intervention, override, recovery, feedback, and control behavior in discovery, concept, field-learning, and production-readiness evidence.

sources.key_finding: Human-centered AI development connects user needs, data and model capabilities, mental models, explainability, feedback, control, errors, and graceful failure throughout product design.
sources.operationalization: Use human-work evidence, calibrated expectations, controllability, recovery, and qualitative research as product requirements rather than post-build polish.

sources.source: NIST SP 800-218 — Secure Software Development Framework 1.1
sources.key_finding: Secure development integrates preparation, protection of software, production of well-secured software, and vulnerability response into the development lifecycle.
sources.operationalization: Require threat/risk work, protected build environments, review and testing, provenance, vulnerability handling, and evidence before release.

sources.source: NIST SP 800-218 Rev. 1 Initial Public Draft
sources.key_finding: The evolving SSDF revision reinforces lifecycle-wide secure software practices and updates implementation considerations for modern development environments.
sources.operationalization: Mark draft-derived guidance as provisional, keep plugin security rules tied to stable principles, and review the source when the standard is finalized.

sources.source: NIST SP 800-218A — Secure Software Development Practices for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models
sources.key_finding: AI software development adds model, data, provenance, evaluation, misuse, supply-chain, and deployment risks that should be integrated into secure development practices.
sources.operationalization: Extend threat models and release evidence to prompts, models, tools, datasets, evaluations, agent permissions, and model/provider changes.

sources.key_finding: Build provenance and progressively stronger build integrity controls make software artifacts traceable to source, build process, and protected infrastructure.
sources.operationalization: Require artifact identity, provenance, reproducible or verifiable build steps, protected release credentials, and exact delivered-artifact checks.

sources.key_finding: CycloneDX provides machine-readable BOM models for components, services, dependencies, vulnerabilities, attestations, and other supply-chain information.
sources.operationalization: Generate and validate an SBOM or equivalent inventory for release where appropriate and link it to artifact provenance and vulnerability policy.

sources.key_finding: Software manufacturers should make secure outcomes the default, reduce customer security burden, treat security as a core product requirement, and improve transparency and accountability.
sources.operationalization: Make secure defaults, least privilege, safe failure, product-level security outcomes, and ownership explicit from discovery through maintenance.

sources.source: CISA — Software Bill of Materials resources
sources.key_finding: An SBOM is a formal component inventory that supports vulnerability identification, risk assessment, transparency, and coordinated response across the software lifecycle.
sources.operationalization: Require release and maintenance processes to retain component inventory, ownership, update policy, and linkages to vulnerability response and retirement.

sources.source: Google SRE — Evolving SRE Engagement Model / Production Readiness Review
sources.key_finding: A production readiness review examines architecture, dependencies, capacity, failure modes, monitoring, alerts, runbooks, rollout, and operational ownership before service handoff or launch.
sources.operationalization: Require a production-readiness evidence package with owners, SLOs, capacity, dependencies, failure/recovery tests, observability, runbooks, rollout, and rollback.

sources.key_finding: Service-level objectives and error budgets translate reliability into an explicit risk and investment decision, balancing reliability work against product velocity.
sources.operationalization: Define SLIs/SLOs and an error-budget policy with release, escalation, experimentation, and remediation consequences rather than treating reliability as a slogan.

sources.key_finding: Effective incident response uses clear command roles, communication, operational coordination, escalation, and disciplined recovery under pressure.
sources.operationalization: Require incident roles, severity, escalation, containment, communication, evidence capture, and recovery/reconciliation procedures for consequential agent systems.

sources.key_finding: Blameless postmortems focus on contributing system conditions, impact, timeline, detection, response, and owned corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
sources.operationalization: Turn incidents and field failures into mechanism-based learning records, owned corrections, regression evidence, and follow-through checks rather than anecdotes or blame.

sources.source: Google SRE — Reliable Product Launches at Scale
sources.key_finding: Reliable launches depend on repeatable launch reviews, explicit risk criteria, capacity and dependency checks, monitoring, rollback, and organizational learning from prior launches.
sources.operationalization: Use a launch evidence package and progressive rollout contract, not calendar pressure or code completion, as the basis for production exposure.

sources.key_finding: Canarying limits exposure while comparing a new version with a baseline and requires representative traffic, useful metrics, enough observation time, and automated or explicit rollback criteria.
sources.operationalization: Define cohorts, exposure steps, guardrails, analysis windows, hold/advance/revert rules, and effect containment for agent releases.

sources.key_finding: Reliable releases are reproducible, automated, self-service where safe, auditable, and built from well-defined source and build inputs.
sources.operationalization: Require deterministic release pipelines, artifact provenance, controlled permissions, repeatable rollback, and release evidence independent of a developer session.

sources.key_finding: Reliability requires layered tests including unit, integration, system, load, configuration, and failure-oriented testing; no single test class establishes production readiness.
sources.operationalization: Build a verification ladder aligned to quality attributes, dependencies, failure modes, rollout, and exact artifacts; record skipped or unavailable evidence honestly.

sources.key_finding: Software delivery performance should be understood with a balanced set of throughput and stability measures, interpreted in context rather than optimized as isolated targets.
sources.operationalization: Track delivery flow and stability as diagnostics, avoid ranking teams or gaming a composite score, and connect measures to product outcomes and learning speed.

sources.source: Google Cloud — 2025 DORA Report: AI-Assisted Software Development
sources.key_finding: AI assistance can amplify both strengths and weaknesses of a software delivery system; organizational capabilities, feedback quality, platform engineering, and control practices shape outcomes.
sources.operationalization: Treat agent use as a sociotechnical change, measure downstream flow and stability, and invest in repository, platform, evaluation, and feedback infrastructure rather than model access alone.

sources.source: Microsoft Azure Well-Architected Framework — Safe deployment practices
sources.key_finding: Safe deployment reduces blast radius through progressive exposure, health evaluation, bake time, rollback, separation of concerns, and deployment controls.
sources.operationalization: Require ringed rollout, stop/rollback criteria, health and business guardrails, ownership, and recovery evidence; do not confuse a feature flag with authorization.

sources.key_finding: Argo Rollouts supports canary and blue-green strategies, analysis runs, pauses, promotion, and rollback for Kubernetes workloads.
sources.operationalization: Treat rollout controllers as execution mechanisms under a predeclared evidence and authorization contract; keep product decisions outside controller defaults.

sources.key_finding: Flagger automates progressive delivery using service-mesh or ingress traffic shifting, metrics, analysis, promotion, and rollback.
sources.operationalization: Use automated rollout only with trustworthy metrics, minimum exposure, explicit failure handling, and independent authorization for consequential effects.

sources.key_finding: Evaluation context carries targeting information through a feature-evaluation transaction and has defined merge precedence and lifecycle semantics.
sources.operationalization: Version rollout context, distinguish assignment from exposure, propagate stable non-sensitive identifiers, and record evaluated variant and reason with field evidence.

sources.key_finding: Targeting context may contain sensitive information and should be minimized, protected, and handled consistently across providers and hooks.
sources.operationalization: Ban raw sensitive content from default rollout context, use allowlists and pseudonymous stable IDs, and document retention and access policy.

sources.key_finding: The Rust SDK provides a vendor-neutral feature-flag API with evaluation context, providers, hooks, and typed evaluation details.
sources.operationalization: Keep feature evaluation behind a Rust adapter, propagate context explicitly, expose reason/error details to telemetry, and do not treat flags as permission checks.

sources.key_finding: Rust tracing models structured, contextual diagnostics as spans and events, supporting async-aware instrumentation and subscriber-based collection.
sources.operationalization: Instrument run/action/tool/effect/approval/recovery boundaries with stable domain IDs, propagate spans through owned tasks, and keep event fields structured.

sources.key_finding: OpenTelemetry Rust provides APIs and SDKs for traces, metrics, logs, context propagation, and export through vendor-neutral telemetry pipelines.
sources.operationalization: Use OTel at system boundaries, bridge tracing context intentionally, test propagation and shutdown/flush behavior, and preserve domain semantics independently of a backend.

sources.key_finding: Observability is the ability to understand internal system state from outputs; instrumentation emits traces, metrics, and logs that serve different but complementary diagnostic purposes.
sources.operationalization: Design telemetry from decisions and failure mechanisms backward, with joinable signals and explicit diagnostic questions rather than indiscriminate logging.

sources.key_finding: Telemetry can capture personal, credential, financial, health, or behavioral data; implementers own minimization, consent, protection, redaction, and review.
sources.operationalization: Apply allowlists, privacy classifications, redaction, bounded retention, access controls, and sampling policies; do not record raw prompts or tool payloads by default.

sources.key_finding: GenAI semantic conventions define evolving common attributes and events for model, agent, and tool telemetry, with stability levels and privacy implications that require review.
sources.operationalization: Adopt stable conventions selectively, namespace product-specific domain fields, version schemas, and avoid relying on experimental attributes as immutable contracts.

sources.key_finding: Trace Context standardizes propagation of trace identifiers and flags across process and service boundaries while defining interoperability and privacy considerations.
sources.operationalization: Propagate W3C context across agent services and tools, but keep trace identity separate from authorization and from durable business/effect identity.

sources.source: OWASP — AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
sources.key_finding: Agent systems face prompt injection, excessive agency, tool abuse, memory poisoning, data leakage, unsafe output handling, and denial-of-service risks that require layered controls.
sources.operationalization: Carry security constraints into authentic-use operating envelopes, tool contracts, telemetry, approvals, effect integrity, incident response, and release gates.

sources.key_finding: Agentic applications introduce risks around goals, identity and privilege, tool use, memory and context, inter-agent trust, cascading failures, and insufficient monitoring or governance.
sources.operationalization: Use the taxonomy as threat-model prompts and coverage checks, not a substitute for system-specific assets, trust boundaries, misuse cases, and effect analysis.

sources.key_finding: Skills use progressive disclosure; the initial list is bounded and descriptions drive implicit activation.
sources.operationalization: Compress descriptions, retain one host-owned implicit front door, and add context-budget and routing gates.

sources.source: OpenAI — Testing Agent Skills Systematically with Evals
sources.key_finding: Skill evals should cover explicit, implicit, contextual, and negative cases with trace, artifact, outcome, and efficiency checks.
sources.operationalization: Add baseline, routing, JSONL trace, artifact, negative-control, and efficiency evaluation contracts.

sources.key_finding: Leaner prompts and relevant tools can improve quality and efficiency; Pro, Programmatic Tool Calling, reasoning, and multi-agent should be selected by measured task shape.
sources.operationalization: Use one lean outcome contract and move variation into configuration and representative evals.

sources.key_finding: The project operationalizes brainstorm-plan-work-simplify-review-compound, product pulse, resumable dogfood, and risk-selected review.
sources.operationalization: Adopt bounded compounding, field pulse, journey review, and structured review without creating a second authority.

sources.key_finding: The project operationalizes causal debugging, test-first practice, fresh scoped workers, review, fresh verification, and behavior-tested skills.
sources.operationalization: Adopt skill behavior evals, causal repair, fresh evidence packets, and verification gates while rejecting universal ceremony.

sources.key_finding: AI amplifies both strong user focus and feature-factory dysfunction; outcome evidence must remain visible.
sources.operationalization: Add Product Fitness evidence, representative journeys, and user-value measures.

sources.key_finding: Small batches accelerate feedback and amplify positive AI effects on product performance.
sources.operationalization: Use risk-retiring slices and proportional assurance rather than large autonomous batches.

sources.key_finding: Secure access to code, documentation, and operational evidence multiplies individual effectiveness and code quality.
sources.operationalization: Make repository and operational evidence directly legible through bounded context packets.

sources.key_finding: Creation time saved by AI is often reallocated to auditing and verification; throughput can rise with instability.
sources.operationalization: Measure supervisory work and verification burden, not generated output alone.

sources.source: Coding Agents Don’t Know When to Act
sources.key_finding: Agents make undesirable changes on many already-fixed tasks; framing inaction as success improves the design target but partial fixes complicate abstention.
sources.operationalization: Add first-class no-change and partial-change decisions with reproduction evidence.

sources.key_finding: Most repair-loop gains occur in the first three to four iterations; orchestration and feedback strongly influence repair behavior.
sources.operationalization: Require explicit empirically calibrated budgets and circuit breakers.

sources.source: Structured Feedback Improves Repair in an LLM Agent Loop
sources.key_finding: Feedback with failure location, observed value, and admissible alternatives markedly improved terminal success in the studied loops.
sources.operationalization: Standardize structured validator-to-repair feedback.

sources.source: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents
sources.key_finding: Trace normalization and layer-aware attribution enabled scoped harness repairs with held-out improvements.
sources.operationalization: Add responsible-layer attribution and held-out harness repair validation.

sources.key_finding: Test-impact context reduced regressions while procedural TDD prompting alone increased them in the studied setup.
sources.operationalization: Choose verification modes by oracle and surface relevant tests rather than prescribing ritual.

sources.key_finding: Visible/hidden splits, semantic mutation, and specification evolution expose prompt and policy regressions.
sources.operationalization: Add held-out, mutation, and evolution skill evals.

sources.key_finding: Browser acceptance-test infrastructure improved generated web-app quality, while mismatched enforcement protocols multiplied cost without benefit.
sources.operationalization: Use journey/browser evidence and select enforcement protocol by model and task behavior.

sources.source: Are Coding Agents Generating Over-Mocked Tests?
sources.key_finding: Agent commits were more likely to add mocks, raising concern that tests may validate mocks instead of real interactions.
sources.operationalization: Require explicit mock policy and representative boundary evidence.

sources.source: Coding Agents are Effective Long-Context Processors
sources.key_finding: Coding agents can use file systems and executable tools to organize and process very large contexts effectively.
sources.operationalization: Use file-based handoffs, bounded maps, and executable retrieval rather than transcript stuffing.

sources.source: The Impact of AI Coding Assistants on Software Engineering
sources.key_finding: Work shifts toward supervisory engineering; perceived productivity can coexist with worsening flow and cognitive load.
sources.operationalization: Measure intervention, review, correction, cognitive load, and retained ownership.

sources.source: Google Research — From Correctness to Collaboration
sources.key_finding: Professional expectations include standards/process, quality/reliability, effective problem solving, and collaboration—not correctness alone.
sources.operationalization: Evaluate collaborative and authority behavior separately from code correctness.

sources.source: Meta-analysis of generative AI on productivity and learning
sources.key_finding: Productivity effects are positive but heterogeneous and smaller in enterprise/open-source contexts; learning effects were not significant.
sources.operationalization: Avoid assuming generated throughput equals system value or retained expertise.

sources.key_finding: Secure identity, authorization, interoperability, and open standards are central to trusted agent adoption.
sources.operationalization: Keep identity, authority, protocol, and effect boundaries explicit.

sources.key_finding: No finite fixed guardrail set is universally robust; red teaming, continuous updates, and resilience are required.
sources.operationalization: Add continuous monitoring, update, impact limitation, and recovery to agent security.

sources.source: NIST — Building Measurement Probes into Agentic AI Ecosystems
sources.key_finding: Agent traceability requires reconstructing tool use and evidence; dynamic verifiers can provide measurement probes.
sources.operationalization: Require trace/evidence joins and independent verifiers for consequential claims.

sources.source: NIST — Identity and Authority of Software Agents
sources.key_finding: Agent access to data, tools, and applications requires explicit identification and authorization controls.
sources.operationalization: Bind worker, reviewer, effect, and authority identities.

sources.key_finding: Secure and reliable development, delivery, and improvement practices should be integrated into any lifecycle model.
sources.operationalization: Keep proportional assurance inside the full lifecycle without weakening mandatory security boundaries.

scope_addendum: Version 3: proportional assurance, no-change decisions, repair circuit breakers, governed learning, skill behavior evals, Product Fitness, typed worker/reviewer evidence, and knowledge lifecycle control.
